documents.evidence: The rack supplies still let someone claim a board before similar bowls arrive. The hand-spaced example, rear access, back lighting, separate stand and named substitute all retain their purposes, including giving staff someone to contact during an absence.

The calendar still shows availability by date, a late driver can reach the keyholder, and a substitute can return chairs on time if the organizer leaves early. The visible repair tag and separate storage, covered drying spot and removable row signs retain their conditions and purposes.

The whistle explains the speakers’ reaction, and captions identify whose writing is quoted as the reading starts. The rewrite keeps the phrasing and name rules, the full muted review for unexplained replies, the title for midway arrivals and both details staff need on the correction slip.

The original asks the host to meet people at the door and offer an escort, with first-time visitors given as a reason. The rewrite directs the offer to newcomers specifically. The invitation and decline, advance dance announcement, low turn, lighting and quiet social break retain their purposes.

Both welcome bakery loaves, but the original says a neighbor without an oven can make an equally interesting introduction. The rewrite says the bread they introduce can be equally interesting. This shifts the reason from what the participant can contribute to the appeal of the loaf.

Tentative public lines and private practice still reduce different barriers to drawing. The viewfinder frames a manageable patch, the location lets a reader find the plant, fallen pods allow close observation without picking, and the occasional pre-tour period offers quiet company.

The original ties the risk of stage-ready clothes entering the alterations pile to clearing the room at the end. The rewrite places that risk at the end of the night, adding a time of day and dropping the explicit clean-up condition. The rail itself and the other fitting arrangements carry over.

Questions at designated tables, demonstrations away from matches, silent clocks and a separate practice set still address the same disruptions and uncertainties. Visitors can gauge occupancy from the door, and a quiet warning before closing lets beginners agree on a stopping point with their opponent.
